title: Andy Razaf hands out 'On Revival Day' in the studio
summary: On May 19, 1930 Razaf brought the music, sang the vocal, and the band recorded it on the spot.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Back to one particular recording, which was a number called "On Revival Day."
Oh, yeah. I remember that very well. Well, don't leave me standing here.
Well, you went in the studio with the Russell band...

Yeah, we was in there recording, making another recording, and Andy Razaf come in with this music under his arm, and passed it out to Russell, and asked him would he record it for him, and naturally, Russell says yes. And he passed out the music, and just taken us unawares, you know what I mean?
Yeah. This was actually on the 19th of May, 1930, in New York.
Yeah, that could be. Very well so. I can't remember that far back.

Yeah. Mmm-hmm. So we recorded it, and Andy did the vocal on it, too. I think it was his number. I think he had written the number, either he or Fats Waller -- I don't know. Because they worked in collaboration with one another. And he sang it, and just like that, just like you hear it, that's it. And that's about as far as I can go.
Razaf gets credit for being the composer.
Yes. He was the composer and vocalist. I know he was the vocalist, because I was there.

Well, I questioned J.C. Higgenbotham on the same matter, and he also remembered just exactly what you've said, that it was Razaf who came in and passed out the music, and you had to record it on the spot.
That's right. Yeah, we didn't get many numbers then you could take home and rehearse on them. They'd pass them out to you and want them right away. And they got it.
